findings.title: Definite retention-budget rejection still strands a native captured responder
findings.verification_status: Static causal proof; no payload or runtime reproduction executed
findings.summary: The new ingress bound proves Grok reply-frame representability, not canonical selection-retention capacity. A small genuine Grok question can be published while other individually in-frame pending forms occupy most of the shared 4-MiB live-interaction budget. A valid 40-KiB Other note passes native/shared validation and fits the reply frame but exceeds the remaining 32-KiB selection-retention headroom. Broker admission rejects before any canonical selection/work/call publication. NativeControl displays the definite capacity error but cannot return the correlated action to the editor. With the same original grant, tuple, interaction and pending disposition, captured remains set and edits/F5/F7 are refused. A smaller deliberate answer or F7 would otherwise fit.

locations.role: Pending/responding details plus proposed selection must fit retained-content budget
Definite rejection before canonical selection/work/call publication
Ingress admits pending detail without reserving a later arbitrary answer selection
Local validation then capture precede daemon admission
Restoration exists only for synchronous local queue rejection
Reply contains target/op/result, not original action identity
Async definite non-admission is displayed but not returned to editor
Only immediate local enqueue error invokes restoration

source_to_failure_trace: [INFERENCE from implemented sizes/control flow, not run] Use one ready owned session with a current original native grant. The adapter serially sends four standard supported session-scoped elicitation forms carrying about 1000000 ASCII description bytes each, a smaller filler form, and a small genuine Grok question. Use distinct bounded RPC IDs and correct session/tool IDs. Tune the filler description so the sum of value_bytes(detail) of all six pending interactions is 4194304 - 32768 = 4161536 bytes. Each individual request stays below1048576 bytes, six responders stay below64, and no writer stall or outstanding-output pressure is required.

Send the next request only after the prior request is canonically inspectable, so transient ingress queue pressure is not necessary. Standard form annotation strings are permitted by validate_form_schema without a smaller length cap; incoming_request checks only current live detail plus new detail. All six can therefore be pending simultaneously.

The native interaction cache explicitly permits the broker's4-MiB detail budget plus512 bytes of generated metadata per record. These six records fit. The small Grok form's q0 and q0_notes controls are supported; question/reply metadata is far under the new489472-byte admission ceiling.

The human deliberately selects Other and supplies40960 ASCII note bytes. The short q0/Other/q0_notes wrapper plus these notes fits the shared65536-byte submitted-values limit, meets nonempty Other notes validation, and yields a small(<1MiB) concrete Grok reply. First F5 validates/reviews; second F5 sets captured and enqueues the small local request.

Authority::admit_acp rechecks the same current grant/generation. Broker commit constructs the canonical CreateElicitationResponse selection containing the40960-byte note. Its serialized size exceeds32768 remaining retention bytes, so state.retain_capacity(selection_bytes) at943 returns capacity-exceeded before the no-fallible-operation publication point at960. The budget rejection itself is correct; no call tombstone/work/selection or answer frame is committed.

NativeControl.poll receives a definite DaemonError, removes the local busy bit, displays the error, and refreshes facts. capacity-exceeded does not invalidate the current grant. Reply carries no original action/call envelope, and no path forwards this negative admission to AgentView.

AgentView.sync sees the same binding and exact pending interaction. sync_interactions discards local capture only when canonical disposition becomes nonpending; authority sync discards only when binding changes. Neither happens. Interaction.editable immediately refuses captured actions, including F7 and field edits.

A short replacement Other note or the tiny cancel selection would fit the available32768 bytes and answer the retained original RPC. Both are blocked by the stale local captured latch. API cancellation or changing authority can work around it; explicit foreground interrupt would alter the whole turn. None is deliberate correction/cancellation of this retained native question on its unchanged original grant.

evidence.label: Independent reachable retention rejection
evidence.explanation: The input need not violate the repaired Grok bound: large supported STANDARD form descriptions occupy retention, while the affected Grok question is small. Pending details cannot be evicted by trim_interactions. Six serial in-frame requests and a40-KiB answer are within all individual schema/count/value limits.
evidence.excerpt: fn retain_capacity(&self, extra: usize) ... filter(|i| i.state == "pending" || i.responding) ... live_bytes + extra <= QUEUE_BYTES

evidence.label: Definite no-admission precedes publication
evidence.explanation: The canonical selection bytes are checked after local capture but before frame enqueue, interaction selection, call-ID insertion and work publication. A caller capacity error does not close/degrade this live instance, so pending state and authority remain unchanged.
evidence.excerpt: state.capacity(&frames, request.is_some())?; ... state.retain_capacity(selection_bytes)?; ... // No fallible operation below this point.

evidence.label: Native capture has only synchronous-rejection restoration
evidence.explanation: The editor records call_id before asynchronous RPC completion. Only acp_action returning Err immediately invokes restore_unqueued; the asynchronous daemon error branch updates status/refresh timing without returning the original action. Unknown timeout/disconnect must remain distinct from this definite non-admission.

evidence.label: Unchanged canonical refresh cannot unlock it
evidence.explanation: sync_interactions retains each item and updates only canonical mutable fields. It calls discard only for !pending. Binding mismatch also discards, but the scenario deliberately retains the same grant/tuple. Neither normal refresh path clears this capture.

findings.impact: A valid published native question becomes noneditable/noncancellable after a correctly rejected answer even though its canonical responder is pending, the original session/turn is alive, and smaller correction/cancel could be admitted. The user must leave the intended native workflow, acquire another authority, use the API or interrupt/close. No false canonical answer, arbitrary execution, permission widening, secret exposure, authority bypass or automatic replay is claimed.
findings.remediation: Propagate definite daemon non-admission with the original call/interaction/revision/target/control/generation to the editor. Only when those identities still match and the canonical interaction remains pending, clear the matching captured/review state and permit a NEW deliberate smaller answer or F7. Do not replay, substitute a later owner, or clear capture on ambiguous timeout/disconnection. Keep resource admission checks intact. Add a deterministic actual-native retained-content rejection followed by same-grant deliberate correction/cancel, exact original RPC, no rejected work/call/wire effect, and owned cleanup before fallback.
findings.why_not_security: The required exclusions remove general DoS/resource pressure as a vulnerability. This is instead the specifically supported operational negative-admission/native-responder failure. There is no proven security-boundary crossing, so it is not labelled a CWE security finding.
findings.root_cause_boundary: Missing exact asynchronous negative-admission feedback into local capture state, not failure of the repaired serialized-reply bound. The retention check correctly rejects. Other writer/call capacity errors may share this missing feedback path, but are not counted as separate findings or claimed independently reproduced.

reply_bound_assessment.verdict: PASS-static for Grok wire-frame representability; does not imply all resource admission succeeds
reply_bound_assessment.formula: P=value_bytes(original params), C=value_bytes(submitted values). Require P <= (1048576 - 65536 - 4096)/2 = 489472. Then2P + C +4096 <=1048576.
reply_bound_assessment.metadata_terms: Each original question string appears at most twice as an encoded map key: answers and optional annotations. A selected single-choice preview is copied once, comes from original params, and is not repeated for multiple selections. Distinct question texts prevent accidental key aliasing. Request-owned question keys/previews together are bounded by2P, including JSON quotes/escapes/UTF-8. Dropped descriptions/options/metadata only make this conservative.
reply_bound_assessment.submitted_terms: Every selected label/string-array entry and note is already present once in the shared serialized values budget C<=65536. Scalar choice to one-element wire array adds only fixed per-question syntax; notes/selected arrays are not multiplied by question count. Per-question qN/qN_notes field names removed from values only reduce the bound. Shared validation checks offered choices/distinct arrays/nonempty Other notes before native review and again at admission.
reply_bound_assessment.overhead_terms: At most32 question records. Structural reply punctuation plus answer scalar-array wrapping and annotation notes/preview keys is comfortably below100 bytes/question excluding strings already charged toP/C, i.e.<3200 bytes. A control-free string RPC ID has at most256 raw UTF-8 bytes and at most512 serialized interior bytes for quotes/backslashes; numeric i64 IDs need at most20 characters, null4. JSON-RPC envelope/outcome/map/newline framing fits the remaining reserve;3200+512+128=3840<4096 is a conservative structural allowance. value_bytes uses serde_json::to_writer with a counting writer, so control-character escaping in question/preview/value strings is actually counted rather than estimated as raw length.
reply_bound_assessment.ordering: validate_rpc_id runs before incoming_request. grok::form applies the bound before constructing returned canonical schema; incoming_request does not insert a responder/interaction until parse and retention/cancellation checks finish. A size error is returned on the exact original RPC as-32602 via error_response, with no canonical/native interaction. Error response egress exhaustion itself fails the connection explicitly rather than fabricating success.
reply_bound_assessment.historical_finding: Historical E04S04-OPS-R5-01's600000-byte question is rejected by the new predicate before schema/responder publication. This report does not repeat that repaired finding.
reply_bound_assessment.remaining_limit: Neither2P+C+4096 nor the current regression proves dynamic retained selection capacity, writer/RPC capacity, or negative-admission editor recovery. E04S04-OPS-S1-01 supplies a separate concrete reachable rejection path.
